input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
errors: Killing the first parity run mid-way skipped its finally-restore, leaving a test pg_hba.conf loaded; restored the admin trust file by hand before re-running.
Container has no IPv6: ::1 connections failed, so they were dropped from the match matrix (IPv6 covered by unit tests and parse parity only).

doc_friction.issue: Tag spelling ('devtools' vs 'dev-tools') and the 70-char seo_title limit surface only through unwired checks and distribution tests, not the venture suite; cost one extra round.
Copied 'every type the engine can emit' test greps any `type: "..."` literal, which also matches non-finding objects (connection types); had to exclude them.

notes: Explore idea: pg-hba-check, a pg_hba.conf checker (PostgreSQL 16 semantics: first match wins, refuse-whole-file, includes, inet_aton addresses, shadowed rules, connection simulation). Parity against real PostgreSQL 16.15 in the container: 600 generated files / 3,583 pg_hba_file_rules rows and 160 files x 36 real connections = 5,760 logins (deciding line from log_connections), 0 differences after fixing a samerole self-membership engine bug (13 diffs) and a harness regex (20 diffs). Local: run_venture_tests.py pg-hba-check pass; unwired_checks failures my diff caused (check_posts seo_title and tag, CLI flag values, distribution tests reading the post) fixed and re-run green; check_trailing_flag_value exits 0 (it notes a stale timber-sale-offer-checker baseline line, left alone). No agent doc: the README and parity/README carry what the next run needs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a security engineer writing a pg_hba.conf parser and matcher from hba.c, a real-server parity harness, tests, two pages and a post: about three days

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
